hardening: Captured Sprint5 recovery_decisions.py is partial and has no tests or public/CLI wiring here. verify_receipt calls OperatorPermits.authenticate, which is absent in captured recovery.py; propose expects original_request_ids/original_occurrence_ids omitted by captured BranchVerifier. Treat these as fail-closed integration limitations, not exploitable vulnerabilities; re-audit after Sprint5 completes.

RecoveryRegistry._validate_reference at recovery_decisions.py:262-265 has a permissive fallthrough for some epoch/head mismatches. Current accepted initialization and next references are additionally compared to guard.trust_reference(current=True), and previous witness is derived from those admitted records, so no untrusted boundary bypass is established. Tighten generation membership before exposing any broader reference-import interface.

Port descriptor-relative all-component ownership/write-permission checks from the infrastructure securefs helper to application enrollment/restore/ledger paths, and pin trusted directory descriptors for publication/SQLite handling. This reduces explicit protected-ancestor assumptions; no other-UID exploit is claimed.

Keep HMAC keys, latest external minimum references, enrollment witness/reservation and registry reference independently custodied with a trustworthy clock. A genesis witness proves its ancestor, not freshness of all later history; coordinated custody rollback and same-UID/key compromise remain outside the documented local contract.
Logical size/row and archive/restore count bounds are not physical SQLite/WAL filesystem quotas. Preserve partial artifacts and plan operator-managed storage/capacity policy before live use.
